members.summary: Configuration for every T5 variant (Raffel et al., 2020, §3.7).
members.extended:
The defaults are T5-Small.  `vocab_size` is the 32 000-piece
SentencePiece vocabulary with 100 sentinels, padded to 32 128 rows.
examples:
>>> from lucid.models.text.t5._config import T5Config
>>> cfg = T5Config()
>>> cfg.model_type
't5'
>>> cfg.hidden_size, cfg.inner_dim, cfg.vocab_size
(512, 512, 32128)
The attention width is num_attention_heads * head_dim, which need
not be the model width:
>>> T5Config(hidden_size=1024, num_attention_heads=32, head_dim=128).inner_dim
4096

members.summary: T5 with its language-modelling head — the model every T5 task trains.
members.extended:
Wraps `T5Model` with a bias-free projection to the vocabulary.
With `config.tie_word_embeddings` (the paper's setting) the
projection *is* the shared token table, and the decoder output is
scaled by $d_{\text{model}}^{-1/2}$ first: the table is drawn at
unit variance for the input side, so the tied output would otherwise
be $\sqrt{d_{\text{model}}}$ too large.

Pass `labels` alone and the decoder input is built from them —
`decoder_start_token_id` followed by the labels shifted right, with
`-100` replaced by the pad id — as the paper's teacher forcing does.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description:
Hyperparameters; `tie_word_embeddings` and
`decoder_start_token_id` shape the head.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.text.t5 import T5Config, T5ForSeq2SeqLM
>>> cfg = T5Config(vocab_size=100, hidden_size=32, num_hidden_layers=2,
...                num_decoder_layers=2, num_attention_heads=4,
...                head_dim=8, intermediate_size=64)
>>> model = T5ForSeq2SeqLM(cfg).eval()
>>> src = lucid.tensor([[13, 5, 42, 1]])
>>> labels = lucid.tensor([[7, 9, 1]])
>>> out = model(src, labels=labels)
>>> out.logits.shape, out.loss.shape
((1, 3, 100), ())
notes:
Reference: Raffel et al., JMLR 2020 ([arXiv:1910.10683](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10683)), §2.1 and §3.1.4.

With `labels` the loss is the mean per-token cross-entropy over
positions not labelled `-100`:



$$
\mathcal{L} = -\frac{1}{|V|} \sum_{(b, t) \in V}
    \log p_\theta(y_{b,t} \mid x_b,\, y_{b,<t}).
$$

attributes.description: `(d_model → vocab_size)` projection, the shared table when tied.

members.extended:
Implements the architecture of Raffel, Shazeer, Roberts, Lee, Narang,
Matena, Zhou, Li and Liu, 2020.  One token table embeds both the
source and the target.  The encoder stack reads the source with
bidirectional attention; the decoder stack reads the target causally
and cross-attends to the encoder output.  Neither side adds a
position to its tokens: each stack's blocks add one learned
per-head bias, indexed by bucketed relative distance, to their
self-attention logits.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description:
Vocabulary, width, depth on each side, head count and width,
relative-position bucketing, dropout and the init scale.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.text.t5 import T5Config, T5Model
>>> cfg = T5Config(vocab_size=100, hidden_size=32, num_hidden_layers=2,
...                num_decoder_layers=2, num_attention_heads=4,
...                head_dim=8, intermediate_size=64)
>>> model = T5Model(cfg).eval()
>>> src = lucid.tensor([[13, 5, 42, 1]])
>>> tgt = lucid.tensor([[0, 7, 9]])
>>> out = model(src, decoder_input_ids=tgt)
>>> out.last_hidden_state.shape, out.encoder_last_hidden_state.shape
((1, 3, 32), (1, 4, 32))
notes:
Reference: Raffel et al., *"Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning
with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer"*, JMLR 21(140), 2020
([arXiv:1910.10683](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10683)), §2.1 and §3.1.

Head $h$ of every block scores query $i$ against key
$j$ as



$$
A_{ij} = q_i^{\top} k_j + b_{h,\,\beta(j - i)},
$$

unscaled, and every sub-layer $f$ updates the stream as
$x \leftarrow x + f\bigl(x / \mathrm{RMS}(x) \odot \gamma\bigr)$.

attributes.name: shared
attributes.description: The `(vocab_size, d_model)` table both stacks embed with.

attributes.name: decoder
attributes.description: Causal stack of `num_decoder_layers` blocks with cross-attention.

>>> from lucid.models.text.t5._model import T5ModelOutput
>>> out = T5ModelOutput(
...     last_hidden_state=lucid.zeros(2, 7, 512),

notes: Reference: Raffel et al., JMLR 2020 ([arXiv:1910.10683](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10683)), §2.4 and §3.7.

summary: T5 family — Raffel et al., 2020 (text-to-text encoder-decoder).
citation: Raffel, Colin, et al. "Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer." Journal of Machine Learning Research, vol. 21, no. 140, 2020, pp. 1–67.
theory:
T5 casts every task — translation, summarisation, classification,
regression — as **text in, text out**: a task prefix such as
`"summarize: "` is prepended to the input and the answer is decoded
as tokens, so one encoder-decoder, one loss and one decoding procedure
serve them all.

**Relative position bias.**  No position is added to the tokens.
Each attention head instead adds a learned scalar to its logits,
looked up by the bucketed distance $j - i$ from query to key:



$$
A_{ij} = q_i^{\top} k_j + b_{h,\,\beta(j - i)},
$$

with **no** $1/\sqrt{d_{kv}}$ scaling — the Mesh TensorFlow
initialisation folds it into the query projection.  The bucket map
$\beta$ is exact for the $m$ nearest distances and
logarithmic beyond, saturating at `relative_attention_max_distance`
$D$.  For $n$ buckets per direction and $m = n/2$,



$$
\beta(r) =
\begin{cases}
    |r| & |r| < m, \\
    \min\!\Bigl(n - 1,\; m + \Bigl\lfloor
        \dfrac{\log(|r| / m)}{\log(D / m)}\,(n - m)
    \Bigr\rfloor\Bigr) & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
$$

The encoder splits its 32 buckets between the two signs of
$r$ ($n = 16$); the causal decoder uses all 32 for
$r \le 0$.  One table per stack, computed once and shared by
every layer.

**Simplified layer norm.**  Every sub-layer reads
$x / \mathrm{RMS}(x) \odot \gamma$ — no mean subtraction, no
bias — and adds its output back to the unnormalised stream
(pre-norm residual), with a final norm closing each stack.

**Objective.**  Pre-training corrupts 15% of the input tokens in
spans of mean length 3, replaces each span with a unique sentinel
and asks the decoder for the dropped spans, each after its sentinel.
Every task then trains the same per-token cross-entropy



$$
\mathcal{L} = -\sum_{t} \log p_\theta(y_t \mid x,\, y_{<t}),
$$

the decoder reading the target shifted right behind
`decoder_start_token_id`.  The paper's five sizes span 60M to 11B
parameters; T5-11B set the state of the art on GLUE, SuperGLUE,
SQuAD and CNN/Daily Mail at publication.
